overview.title: AIZK becomes mb memory: one PostgreSQL, one DuckLake, one login
overview.owner_request: Let's try to start organizing things to unify aizk into mb memory, so all runs from the same ducklake + pg system. (owner, 2026-10-10)

extends.design: mainboard refactor design v3 (revision c97cb81), /Users/pedro/Developer/mb-refactor/refactor/design.json, packages M00 to M38
inherits: one center PostgreSQL cluster on the internal disk, run by mainboard from the workspace environment, never a system install (Q01)
database mainboard with schema control and one ducklake_<LakeId> schema per lake; Parquet and blobs under the lake DATA_PATH on /Volumes/PORTABLE
drain-and-switch for every live change, a measured 60 s final write pause where a switch is mechanical (Q10), one host-wide card lease for every user of an owned card (Q05)
implementation agents edit only designated worktrees and never deploy; the lead applies live switches; no commit or push without the owner

overview.goal: AIZK keeps its public identity (separate repository, MCP contract, Logto login) but its data, its services and its history live on the same system as mainboard: the center's single PostgreSQL cluster holds the DuckLake catalog, the control schema and AIZK's transactional data in separate databases; AIZK's append-only history and logs land in the same DuckLake the evidence lives in; the `mb memory` front, the doctor and the backups treat AIZK as part of the center. crimson stops serving AIZK and its GPU 0 returns to the lease pool.
overview.recommended_layout: One cluster, three databases (mainboard, aizk, logto), roles that cannot cross databases, extensions limited to what conda-forge carries on osx-arm64, linux-64 and linux-aarch64 (contrib plus pgvector 0.8.6), data directory on the internal disk, offsite backups on crimson's empty SSD.
overview.recommended_placement: The center Mac mini hosts the PostgreSQL cluster and AIZK's whole application tier (MCP server, API, worker, Caddy, Logto, cloudflared) as launchd services from the workspace environment, with containers only for software that has no conda-forge build. Embeddings and reranking move to OpenRouter behind a golden-set gate. crimson keeps the old stack stopped for rollback, then becomes the backup target.
key_evidence: round trip center to crimson over ssh through the cvlab jump: p50 11.5 to 12.0 ms, p90 14.6 to 16.4 ms, p99 about 100 ms; bulk 10.8 to 14 MB/s (measured 2026-10-10)
one find is about 8 to 10 SQL statements, server-side p50 4,954 ms; one keep p50 280 ms; the worker alone issued 5.27 M dequeue statements in 48 days
AIZK database 2,756 MB (tables 2,746 MB, indexes 1,687 MB), 251,821 halfvec(1024) vectors, 5,572 usage events, 659 MB of blobs; live containers total 25.4 GiB of RAM and 20.2 GB of GPU 0

the workspace environment already holds PostgreSQL 18.6; a throwaway cluster from it served a DuckLake catalog in a schema beside control and memory schemas (30 catalog tables, 2.3 ms single-row commits) and loaded conda-forge pgvector 0.8.6 through PostgreSQL 18 extension_control_path
VectorChord 1.1.1, vchord_bm25 0.3.0 and pg_tokenizer 0.1.1 have no macOS binaries and no conda-forge package; PostgreSQL built-in text search does not segment Japanese (measured)
OpenRouter now lists qwen3-reranker-8b at $0.20 per million tokens and qwen3-embedding-8b at $0.01; a full re-embed is about $0.25
the center's internal disk is 94% full (28 GiB free); its Wi-Fi hop shows 74 ms spikes
none of SERVE's phases has landed; crimson's stack still cannot restart cleanly (five bind mounts into a deleted path)
conventions: ids U00 onward extend M00 to M38; a package fits one Codex run in a designated worktree (packages/aizk worktree for repo=aizk, the refactor worktree for repo=mainboard)

acceptance runs against a throwaway PostgreSQL started from the workspace environment (M00 postgres_cluster fixture, M36 binaries) and fake services; no acceptance item needs crimson, OpenRouter, Cloudflare or the lake volume, except where a package is marked touches_live_state
mainboard.toml edits are delivered as reviewed rollout inputs, never edited by an implementation agent (the monorepo checkout is live)
AIZK never imports mainboard or DuckDB; mainboard never imports AIZK except the client extra behind `mb memory`

no backwards compatibility in the end state: the extension-free path replaces the vendor-extension path once its gate passes and the cutover has soaked (U18 deletes the loser); CockroachDB code is deleted. Until the cutover, both index backends and both lexical backends coexist because the crimson stack must keep running the vendor path while the center stack is rehearsed

two builds are in flight: the L0 build for crimson (U02, U10, U09, U08, merged first and cut as a release) and the center build (everything). The keep journal and maintenance mode are the compatibility surface between them, so they live in the L0 build and are never changed afterwards

Alembic revision numbers are written as <next> in packages and assigned by the lead at integration in the order of order.u_waves[0].internal_order; packages that add a migration declare conflicts_with for each other

server.cluster: one PostgreSQL 18.x cluster per center_id, PGDATA <center-state>/services/postgresql/18/data on the internal disk, binaries from the frozen workspace environment (M36), launchd agent independent of the settler
server.listen: unix socket in a short owned directory (macOS sockaddr_un limit is 103 bytes; the scratchpad path failed in the spike) plus 127.0.0.1 TCP only if a container needs it

tuning_profile_24gb.note: values render from one RAM budget number in mainboard.toml; a restore must run with PGOPTIONS raising maintenance_work_mem (measured 192.8 s default against 117.7 s tuned)

extensions: vector 0.8.6 (conda-forge, created once by the bootstrap role)

databases.name: logto
databases.owned_by_package: U11 and U17 (moved as a dump)

per-role statement_timeout, lock_timeout, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and CONNECTION LIMIT: aizk_app 40, aizk_admin 10, mainboard_rw 20, ducklake_writer 20, logto* 10

extensions.policy: AIZK runs on contrib plus pgvector. VectorChord, vchord_bm25 and pg_tokenizer are not required on the center
extensions.vector_index: pgvector HNSW on halfvec(1024), m 16, ef_construction 64, iterative_scan relaxed_order for RLS-filtered scans
extensions.lexical_lane: application-side llmlingua2 tokens in chunk.lexical, simple tsvector GIN index with ts_rank_cd, pg_trgm word_similarity for titles and short queries
extensions.gate: U03 and U04 acceptance plus the U16 golden-set comparison; if the gate fails, tier 2 builds the three pgrx extensions from source into an extension_control_path directory owned by M36, tier 3 keeps the aizk database on Linux

packages.title: Run AIZK's suite on a throwaway extension-free PostgreSQL
changes: Replace the assumption of a developer PostgreSQL on localhost:5433 with M00's lazy postgres_cluster fixture: initdb from the workspace environment, short owned socket directory, collision-safe port, real fsync, stopped and reaped in finalizers

Supply pgvector 0.8.6 to the fixture through extension_control_path and dynamic_library_path from an unpacked conda-forge package until the workspace pins pgvector (M36 rollout input), so the fixture works before and after that pin

Add marker vendor_pg for tests that need vchord, vchord_bm25 or pg_tokenizer; auto-skip with a named reason when absent and commit the generated list (tests/vendor_pg.txt) so U03 and U04 can drive its count to zero
Keep pytest-xdist isolation: each worker gets its own database on the one cluster; the opt-in external DSN path stays for CI but refuses ports and data directories that are not temporary
Do not lower the 100 percent branch-coverage gate; the fixture itself is covered by a test
acceptance: `mb run test-aizk` completes on the throwaway cluster with no Docker and no network; every non-vendor_pg test passes; the vendor_pg count and list are recorded in the report
a negative test shows the fixture refuses a DSN on port 5433 and a data directory outside its temporary root
four xdist workers get four isolated databases; killing a worker with SIGKILL still leaves no postmaster, no socket directory and no listener after teardown
suite wall time on the fixture is recorded and not more than 1.5 times the current Docker-based run
a macOS and a Linux run both pass (socket path length asserted on both)
packages.risk: low: test infrastructure only; the risk is a hidden dependency on vendor extensions in tests not yet marked
packages.run_scope: temporary roots only; no crimson, no live DSN
packages.proposed_commit: test(aizk): run the suite on an environment-owned throwaway PostgreSQL

packages.title: Golden set, scorer and benchmark job from the operator reports
changes: Define GoldenCase (id, query, intent current|historical|external, expected document ids, forbidden document ids, source report id, failure class) with the six failure classes of SERVE.md's audit table

Builder reads an export of the aizk:reports documents (a read-only SQL export supplied by the lead as data) and emits cases; anything it cannot resolve to expected ids goes to unresolved.jsonl and is never guessed
Scorer: recall@1/5/10/20, MRR, nDCG through ir-measures (already carried), per-class breakdown, paired bootstrap confidence intervals through the statistics stack already in the dev group
Runner `aizk-eval golden run --target URL|DSN` submits as an mb job and writes per-case rows and aggregates as receipts through the existing receipt path; result schema is versioned
New code uses cyclopts, not fire
acceptance: from a fixture of 40 synthetic report documents the builder yields exactly the expected cases and lists the others as unresolved (golden-file test)
scorer output equals ir-measures on a scripted run to 1e-9
the bootstrap interval contains the true paired difference in at least 93 percent of 200 synthetic experiments
a fake MCP server returning scripted rankings produces a receipt with per-case rows; running it twice yields the same receipt hash
reported, not asserted: with the lead's export at least 150 cases and at least 10 per failure class
packages.risk: medium: the quality of the cases decides every later gate; the export is the lead's input
packages.run_scope: temporary roots and fake MCP; the baseline capture against the live stack is live event L-1, run by the lead
packages.proposed_commit: feat(aizk): golden retrieval set and scorer from the operator reports

packages.title: Retrieval fixes from SERVE phase 0
changes: Title authority only for distinctive titles: two or more words or an identifier, and unique among the caller's visible documents
A document id named in a query gets direct authority and returns the full source; add a read-by-id path for whole documents
The reports scope is excluded from find unless the caller names it
Supersession: prefer the newest document per (project, kind) for DEV LOG, TODO and handoff; stronger recency when the query says current or latest; a correction closes the claims it refutes
The overview lane gets a fixed share of the budget; add a source prior (authored private over organization over imported)
Each rule is one typed term in the existing single find statement, with its own setting and a test; no second code path
acceptance: unit tests on the throwaway PostgreSQL with fixed vectors: a one-word title 'latest' does not outrank a distinctive match; a bare document id returns that document; reports never surface without the scope; a correction retires the refuted claim; an overview cannot exceed its share
against the golden set (fixture corpus here, real corpus at U16) every failure class improves with a paired-bootstrap p below 0.05 and no class loses more than 0.01 MRR
the single-statement property holds: the find program still compiles to one cached Select
branch coverage gate unchanged
packages.risk: medium: ranking changes are the product; mitigated by the golden set and per-class gates
packages.run_scope: temporary PostgreSQL and fake model lanes; deployment is live event L0
packages.proposed_commit: fix(aizk): phase 0 retrieval fixes from the operator report audit

packages.title: pgvector HNSW as the vector backend, with conversion of an existing database
changes: Make index_backend hnsw first-class: parameters m, ef_construction, hnsw.ef_search, hnsw.iterative_scan relaxed_order so an RLS-filtered scan still returns the requested depth

required_extensions for hnsw with the fts lexical backend is vector, pg_trgm, pgcrypto only; the migration creates vchord, vchord_bm25 and pg_tokenizer only when a vendor backend is selected. vchordrq stays selectable until U18 deletes it, because the crimson stack runs it until the cutover

`aizk admin database convert --to hnsw`: drop the five vchordrq indexes, build HNSW per table with maintenance_work_mem and parallel workers set for the session, validate counts and index validity, resumable per table

`aizk admin database restore-plan DUMP`: write a pg_restore -L list that skips the vendor extensions, the vchordrq and bm25 indexes, the bm25 column, its trigger and the tokenizer objects, so a dump taken from the live vendor-extension database restores into an extension-free cluster; `convert` then builds the HNSW and text-search indexes. Embeddings are untouched (re-embedding is U08)
The SQL stays the same typed statement; only the index operator class and session settings differ
acceptance: fresh `alembic upgrade head` succeeds on the throwaway cluster that has only contrib and pgvector

a fixture dump with the vendor schema (supplied once by the lead from crimson's aizk_bench database, benchmark data only, trimmed to 5,000 rows per vector table, committed under tests/fixtures) restores with the generated -L list into the extension-free cluster without errors, converts, and keeps embeddings bit-for-bit and row counts equal

HNSW recall@50 against an exact scan is at least 0.98 on each of the five tables over 200 queries at RLS selectivities 1, 10 and 100 percent, and the filtered scan returns at least 50 rows whenever 50 are visible
dense-lane statement p50 on a 100,000-row fixture is at most 50 ms (measured 3 ms top-50 on random data)
the vendor_pg count from U00 falls by the number of tests that were only blocked by the vector backend
conversion wall time for 251,821 vectors is measured at U16 and must be at most 12 minutes tuned
packages.risk: high: replaces the dense retrieval index; gate is recall against exact search and the golden set
packages.run_scope: temporary PostgreSQL and a committed fixture dump (one read-only pg_dump of aizk_bench by the lead); real-corpus numbers come from U16
packages.proposed_commit: feat(aizk): pgvector HNSW backend and in-place conversion

packages.title: Lexical lane without vendor extensions
changes: Tokenize in the application with the same llmlingua2 tokenizer the bm25 index used (HF tokenizers, files pinned by hash) into chunk.lexical; index with a simple tsvector GIN; rank with ts_rank_cd; use pg_trgm word_similarity for titles and short queries
Query-side tokenization is the same function; deterministic across macOS and Linux
Backfill command for the 33,268 existing chunks, resumable, run before the HNSW cut at U16

New setting lexical_backend (bm25 or fts); default stays bm25 until the cutover, fts is what the center runs. Both branches stay until U18 deletes the loser (the bm25 column, trigger, index and the vchord_bm25 and pg_tokenizer requirements if fts passed its gate; the fts branch if it failed and tier 2 is built)
acceptance: 60-case Japanese, English and mixed fixture (including identifiers, UUIDs, titles like 'ファンド 基準価額'): top-3 hit rate not more than 0.02 below the bm25 branch on the same fixture, run once with the vendor extensions present for the comparison and once without
index size at most 150 MB per 33,000 chunks (bm25 today: 460 MB), measured
ingest throughput drop at most 10 percent
golden-token test: the tokenizer output for 20 strings is identical on macOS arm64 and Linux x86-64
vendor_pg count reaches zero when the suite is run with index_backend hnsw and lexical_backend fts
packages.risk: high: lexical quality in Japanese is the main reason the vendor extensions were chosen; the fixture comparison and U16 golden run are the gate
packages.run_scope: temporary PostgreSQL; tokenizer files from the Hugging Face cache read-only
packages.proposed_commit: feat(aizk): application-tokenized lexical lane on built-in text search

packages.title: Drop CockroachDB support
changes: Delete the DatabaseBackend switch and every cockroachdb branch (29 source files, 86 mentions), the portable worker and the queue_task, queue_event and queue_schedule tables (empty on PostgreSQL), scoped_cspann and the four CockroachDB revisions, the AWS commands, infra/aws, hackathon/, the CockroachDB deploy files and the nine tests and nineteen doc pages that exist for them
Drop sqlalchemy-cockroachdb, boto3, mangum and aws-cdk from dependencies; remove ccloud, infra, aws and queue-steward tasks as a mainboard.toml rollout input
The lead tags the repository (cockroachdb-profile-final) before the deletion lands; the hackathon profile stays reachable from the tag
PgQueuer becomes the only queue; the Queue wrapper loses its backend conditionals
acceptance: `rg -i cockroach` finds nothing outside CHANGELOG.md and the archive note
`git diff --shortstat` shows at least 8,000 deleted lines (infra 970, hackathon 5,579, deploy 367, source about 1,480, plus tests and docs)
import-linter contracts, ruff, the three type checkers and the branch-coverage gate pass on the U00 fixture
alembic head is identical on a fresh database and on a restored live-shaped database; migration 0019 is a no-op on data
at least four packages leave the dependency lock; the docs site builds with no dangling link
packages.risk: low to medium: large deletion, no behavior change on PostgreSQL; owner decision D2
packages.run_scope: AIZK worktree only; the public repository change is the owner's to push
packages.proposed_commit: refactor(aizk): remove the CockroachDB and AWS profile

packages.title: Object bytes on a local content-addressed store instead of SeaweedFS
changes: ByteStore over obstore LocalStore rooted at AIZK_OBJECT_ROOT; write to a temporary file, fsync, atomic rename; key layout <2 hex>/<content hash>; zstd encoding and the retirement table unchanged
Remove ByteStore.download_url (no caller) and the S3 access-key, secret and endpoint settings; no S3 variant remains

`aizk admin storage import-s3 --endpoint ... --verify`: copy every blob row's object from the old SeaweedFS endpoint, verify size and content hash against blob.content_hash, resumable, idempotent, reports unverifiable objects without deleting anything
Delete the objects service from the compose file
acceptance: put, get, delete, compaction and retirement tests pass on LocalStore; a SIGKILL between write and rename leaves no partial object visible
import of a fake S3 holding 480 objects (including corrupted and missing ones) copies exactly the verifiable ones, lists the others, and a second run changes nothing
two concurrent writers of the same content produce one object
disk usage of the store equals the sum of stored_size within 1 percent on the fixture
packages.risk: low: 480 immutable objects, 659 MB; hash-verified copy
packages.run_scope: temporary directories and an in-process fake S3
packages.proposed_commit: feat(aizk): local content-addressed byte store replaces SeaweedFS

packages.title: Telemetry to files and a usage spool for the lake
changes: Remove the five opentelemetry packages and every exporter, and the observability compose profile with its configuration directory
loguru JSON sink with rotation to AIZK_LOG_DIR; fields ts, level, event, request_id, scopes_hash, operation, duration_ms

Spool: after each usage_event commit append one JSON line (capture_key, all columns) to an atomic segment file in AIZK_SPOOL_DIR; at-least-once, idempotent on capture_key; bounded by size and age, never blocking a keep when the disk is full (drop with a counter exposed in operator_snapshot)
usage_event stays in PostgreSQL as the serving ledger; nothing reads the spool inside AIZK
acceptance: SIGKILL between commit and spool append, then restart: the event reaches the spool exactly once after the recovery pass (property test over 200 random kill points)
every log line parses as JSON with the required keys; no module imports opentelemetry (import-linter forbidden contract)
status, /api/usage and /api/admin/usage return unchanged results on the existing fixtures
with the spool directory at its size cap, 100 keeps still succeed and the drop counter equals the dropped lines
compose profile list no longer contains tempo, loki, victoriametrics, alloy or grafana
packages.risk: low: no data path change; loses Grafana dashboards by design (owner decision D8)
packages.run_scope: temporary directories and PostgreSQL
packages.proposed_commit: refactor(aizk): structured logs and a usage spool replace the observability stack

packages.title: Model lanes without a local GPU: hosted embedding and reranking, optional gate, re-embed
changes: Embedding client accepts an OpenAI-compatible hosted endpoint with the dimensions parameter; at startup it embeds a probe string and refuses to serve if the returned dimension is not embed_dim (1024), so a provider that ignores dimensions cannot silently corrupt the index
Rerank client uses the existing openrouter request format against a hosted reranker; on timeout or error the fused order is returned and the trace records rerank=skipped, never an error to the agent

Extraction gate defaults off (extraction_gate_enabled false); the GLiNER mention detector loads lazily on CPU only when web search is enabled (the ledger shows zero web operations ever); delete the gliner service, vllm-emb, vllm-rerank and docling from the compose file

`aizk admin reembed --backend NAME --resume`: write new vectors into shadow columns of all five vector tables in batches with a token and cost estimate printed first, build the shadow indexes with the active index backend (vchordrq or hnsw), validate parity statistics against the old vectors on a sample, then one `reembed swap` transaction renames the shadow columns and indexes into place for all five tables together and switches the query embedder setting at the same moment. Queries and stored vectors must live in one space, so the swap cannot be per table. Rows written while the job runs are picked up by a final catch-up pass keyed on (id, text hash); resumable and idempotent
Migration <next>_embedding_shadow adds the nullable shadow columns; the swap drops the old columns after a retention period set by the lead
No GPU is required by any default code path
acceptance: a fake embedding server returning 2048-dimensional vectors makes startup fail with a named error; one returning 1024 passes
a fake reranker that times out leaves find answering with the fused order and a trace marker; p99 added latency is bounded by the configured timeout

re-embedding a 2,000-row fixture spread over the five tables is killed three times at random points and finishes with exactly one vector per row; rows inserted while it runs are covered by the catch-up pass; the swap is one transaction over all five tables (a concurrent find sees either all old vectors with the old embedder or all new ones with the new embedder, never a mix; tested with 50 concurrent finds across the swap)
the same re-embed and swap tests pass with index_backend vchordrq on a vendor-extension cluster (marked vendor_pg) and with hnsw on the throwaway cluster
the printed token estimate for the fixture is within 5 percent of the tokens the fake server counted
`docker compose config` of the default profile lists no GPU reservation and no gliner, docling, vllm service
reported at U16 and not asserted here: golden-set MRR and recall@10 of hosted lanes against the local lanes, find p50 against the current 4,954 ms, and the monthly cost at the 30-day load
packages.risk: high: changes the vector space (all 251,821 vectors are re-embedded) and sends note text to a provider; gated by the golden set and owner decision D6
packages.run_scope: fake OpenAI-compatible servers; no provider call in tests
packages.proposed_commit: feat(aizk): hosted embedding and reranking lanes, optional gate, resumable re-embed

packages.title: Worker memory and queue churn
changes: Replace the per-minute per-scope fan-out (about 47,500 chunk and 47,500 artifact dispatch tasks a day) with one dispatch task per tick that scans due scope sets inside one transaction
Aggregate or prune pgqueuer_log on a retention (default 7 days); start the statistics aggregation that is not running (pgqueuer_statistics has 0 rows)
Fix the weekly raptor schedule (last run 2026-08-02) and give failed jobs a retention rule instead of leaving 79 failed rows
Profile the worker (tracemalloc or memray) under a replayed workload and remove the top retained structures; the live process holds 5.62 GiB
acceptance: 33 idle scope sets for one simulated hour produce at most 200 queue rows and log rows (about 11,900 today); dequeue statements at most 0.2 per second
pgqueuer_log never exceeds its retention window in a time-travel test
worker resident set after replaying 5,000 chunks plus graph build and communities is at most 2.0 GiB, with the heap profile committed
the raptor job fires on its cron in a clock-controlled test
no change to job semantics: the existing background tests and coverage gate pass
packages.risk: medium: touches the scheduler every job depends on; mitigated by the existing background suite
packages.run_scope: temporary PostgreSQL and clock control
packages.proposed_commit: fix(aizk): one dispatch tick, a bounded queue log and a smaller worker

packages.title: Maintenance mode and the keep journal
changes: maintenance state in PostgreSQL with modes serving, draining and frozen, read by every transport on each call (cached for at most one second)

draining: keep, share and report fail with a typed retryable error and a retry-after (never acknowledged); find keeps answering but skips access-count updates and writes its usage event to the journal file; background jobs pause; in-flight keeps finish before the mode reports drained
keep_journal: append-only table written in the same transaction as every acknowledged keep, share and report (user id, arguments, resulting ids, capture key)

`aizk admin journal replay --since T --into DSN`: replays through Memory with the recorded user, idempotent on capture key and content hash; `aizk admin maintenance drain|freeze|serve` with a drained check
status reports the mode so an agent sees why a keep was refused
acceptance: property test over 200 runs: random SIGKILLs of the server while 100 concurrent keeps run and the mode flips to draining; the set of acknowledged keeps equals the set of rows in documents, and every one has a journal row
replaying a journal twice onto a second throwaway database yields identical rows (digest equal)
during draining 50 concurrent finds succeed, bump no access counters, and their usage lines are all present in the journal file
a draining server returns the typed retryable error for keep, share and report within 100 ms
drained is reported only after the last in-flight transaction ends (a stalled keep holds it for exactly its duration)
packages.risk: medium: touches the write path of the product; additive table and a mode check
packages.run_scope: temporary PostgreSQL; deployment to crimson is live event L0
packages.proposed_commit: feat(aizk): maintenance modes and a keep journal for loss-free moves

packages.title: Live migration orchestrator and the cutover
changes: `mb memory migrate`: a journaled state machine in the style of M32's switch journal: preflight, drain, freeze, dump, copy, restore, verify, start, route flip, verify gate, thaw, soak; every state resumable or reversible; no step infers success from absence
route.py: Cloudflare tunnel route flip through the API with a manual-confirm fallback; hostnames aizk, auth, admin, console move together; tokens read from the environment and never logged
Verification: per-table counts and id digests, alembic head, doctor probe (keep and find), five golden queries, Logto login through the new issuer path, journal reconciliation
Abort rules: restore not finished by T0 plus 20 minutes, any digest mismatch, or doctor probe red: thaw the old side and stop
Rollback command: freeze the new side, flip routes back, replay the new side's keep journal onto the old side, thaw the old side
Logto moves last (stop, dump, restore, start, flip) so refresh tokens issued during the freeze are not lost
acceptance: against two throwaway PostgreSQL servers, fake services and a fake route endpoint: kill the orchestrator at every state boundary and 300 random points while a keep generator runs; afterwards the set of acknowledged keeps equals the set of rows on the authoritative side and the journal replay reproduces any acknowledged keep missing from it (zero lost)
the write freeze measured on the fixture scaled by the U16 factors stays at most 25 minutes; the read outage (route flip window) at most 2 minutes
rollback after the flip returns the old side to a state containing every keep acknowledged by either side, within a measured 10 minutes
abort at T0 plus 20 minutes thaws the old side with no data change
no secret appears in the journal, logs or reports

migration.principle: move a frozen snapshot, not a moving target; never acknowledge a keep that the surviving side does not hold; keep the old side intact until the new side has been verified and has soaked
scope: FastMCP state files (mcp-state 42 kB, oauth 8 kB)
the public hostnames aizk, auth, admin, console
prerequisites: L0 done: the old side runs the L0 build (draining mode, keep journal); L0.5 done and soaked a week: the vector space is already the hosted one and GPU 0 is idle
L1 done: the center cluster has empty aizk and logto databases, archive_mode on, a verified base backup and offsite copy, AIZK units installed stopped
U16 passed its gates and wrote the freeze budget
wired Ethernet on the center; the center's data volume has at least 15 GiB free after the move
Cloudflare: a tunnel for the center exists with ingress to Caddy and Logto on localhost, tested on a temporary hostname
objects pre-copied with `aizk admin storage import-s3 --verify` (immutable, so safe before the freeze)
a rollback rehearsal on the staging copy passed

steps.action: announce; pre-copy objects; take a rehearsal dump and restore it to staging once more to refresh timings

set draining on the old side: keep, share and report return a typed retryable error (not acknowledged); find continues; background jobs pause; wait for in-flight transactions (at most 30 s) until drained is reported
pg_dump -Fc -j 4 of aizk on crimson (consistent snapshot), checksum, stream to the center (about 350 to 450 MB at 11 to 14 MB/s, 30 to 40 s)
restore into aizk on the center with maintenance_work_mem 1 GB and 4 parallel workers; convert indexes as part of the restore plan; delta of objects added since the pre-copy
verify: alembic head, per-table counts and id digests against the old side, doctor probe on the local route, five golden queries, queue recovery pass for rows left picked
stop Logto on crimson, dump logto, restore on the center, start Logto; flip the four hostnames to the center tunnel; start serving; the read outage is the flip window
set serving on the new side with its keep journal on; replay any usage lines written to the old side's journal file during the freeze; thaw
budget end; anything not done by T0+20 min before the flip aborts the move and thaws the old side

outage_budget.read_outage_note: find is served by the old side until the route flips; the flip window is the only read gap
outage_budget.auth_note: Logto moves last; access tokens already issued stay valid for their lifetime; new sign-ins and refreshes fail only inside the flip window
outage_budget.expected_acknowledged_keeps_affected: at most one: the load is about 1 keep an hour, none is acknowledged during the freeze, the one that arrives gets a retryable error and the agent retries

no_lost_keep: before T0 every acknowledged keep is committed on the old side and therefore in the snapshot
between T0 and the flip no keep is acknowledged: the old side refuses with a typed retryable error, so the agent knows to retry; nothing acknowledged can be missing
after the flip every acknowledged keep is committed on the new side and written to the new side's keep journal in the same transaction
find during the freeze writes nothing the product depends on: access counters are skipped and usage lines go to the journal file and are replayed on the new side (idempotent on capture key)
queue rows left in picked state are recovered by the existing recovery pass; no graph work is lost because the keep itself carries the document and chunks

rollback.before_the_flip: thaw the old side (serve mode); nothing was acknowledged during the freeze, nothing is lost; the center copy is discarded
rollback.after_the_flip_within_24h: freeze the new side (drain), flip the four hostnames back, replay the new side's keep journal onto the old side (idempotent), thaw the old side; every keep acknowledged by either side is present afterwards; budget 10 minutes of write freeze
rollback.after_24h: the old side is stopped; recovery is forward (fix the center) or restore the archived crimson volumes plus replay the journal; the drill for this is part of U18's acceptance
rollback.what_is_retained: the old tunnel, images, volumes and the unchanged crimson database for 24 hours running and 14 days stopped

verification: table counts and per-table digests of ids and last-modified columns equal old and new
forced RLS and the 42 policies present (probe from pg_policies), aizk_app sees nothing without the scope setting
alembic head equals the AIZK release
doctor probe: keep and find as the probe user over the public route
an agent in each of Claude Code, Codex and opencode calls status, find and keep without logging in again (the issuer and its signing keys moved with the logto database)
settler pass latency, free disk and resident set within budget for 24 hours
secrets_and_identity: the AIZK environment file and the Cloudflare tunnel token are the owner's to move into the center's .env (0600, internal disk); rotate the OpenRouter key and the Logto application secrets at the cutover, the new values reach Logto through its own admin API and the .env
issuer https://auth.phvv.me, database, cookie and signing keys are preserved by restoring the logto database as is
what_moves_only_as_a_copy: usage_event (also appended to memory_usage by the spool after the move)
the observability volumes are not migrated (no data worth keeping beyond the usage ledger)
migration.variant_if_freeze_too_long: if U16 measures a freeze above 25 minutes, replace dump and restore by logical replication of the aizk database over an ssh tunnel (publication on crimson, subscription on the center) so the freeze shrinks to the final catch-up; it needs wal_level logical on crimson, i.e. one more database restart inside L0

open_questions.question: Keep AIZK a separate product that mainboard depends on, or merge the repositories? (SERVE decision 2)
open_questions.recommendation: Separate package and repository. Mainboard supervises it and fronts it through `mb memory`. Revisit only if, for a quarter, more than half of AIZK commits also change mainboard.
open_questions.evidence: AIZK is public Apache-2.0 with plugins and PyPI; mainboard ships to Miyabi's 14 GB login node; AIZK 'no longer depends on Mainboard'; the contract needs only a client extra, a spool format and a PostgreSQL layout

open_questions.question: Drop CockroachDB support? (SERVE decision 3)
open_questions.recommendation: Yes: delete it in U05 after tagging the repository. It removes about 8,400 lines (infra 970, hackathon 5,579, deploy 367, source about 1,480), four dependency packages and a second queue; the queue_task tables are empty on PostgreSQL.
open_questions.evidence: state.md section 3 and the grep counts (29 source files, 86 mentions, 9 tests, 19 doc pages)

open_questions.question: Prune crimson's Docker build cache? (SERVE decision 4)
open_questions.recommendation: Yes, but only the cache: `docker builder prune` of entries older than a week is safe now (it touches no image or volume; 223 GB of 289 GB is reclaimable and the root disk is 68% full today, down from 90%). Images stay until the soak ends; volumes follow the archive rehearsal in U18.
open_questions.evidence: docker system df on 2026-10-10: images 112.9 GB, build cache 288.9 GB (223.2 GB reclaimable)

open_questions.question: Where does AIZK run: the center, or stay on crimson with only the database moving?
open_questions.recommendation: The center, as one unit (PostgreSQL plus application tier plus Logto plus the tunnel). Splitting adds 8 to 20 round trips of 12 ms to every call and makes AIZK depend on the Wi-Fi hop and the jump host while both machines are up.
open_questions.evidence: options.md section 2: p50 11.5 ms, 5.27 M dequeue statements in 48 days, keep +85 percent if split

open_questions.question: Which retrieval backend on the shared server?
open_questions.recommendation: Extension-free first (pgvector HNSW plus application-tokenized text search), gated by U03, U04 and the U16 golden run. If the gate fails, build VectorChord, vchord_bm25 and pg_tokenizer from source into an extension_control_path directory (tier 2). Keeping the database on Linux (tier 3) only if both fail.
open_questions.evidence: no conda-forge or macOS binaries for the three vendor extensions; pgvector 0.8.6 on all three platforms; HNSW 75 s and 260 MB per 100k vectors measured; Japanese needs application-side tokens

open_questions.question: Hosted embedding and reranking, or local models?
open_questions.recommendation: Hosted (OpenRouter qwen3-embedding-8b at $0.01 per million tokens, qwen3-reranker-8b at $0.20), behind the golden-set gate on the staging copy, switched on crimson first (live event L0.5) so the cutover moves a stable vector space: it needs no GPU, saves 6.4 GiB of RAM and frees GPU 0, and note text already reaches DeepSeek for extraction under zero-retention terms. Cost at today's load is about $4 a month plus a one-time $0.25 re-embed. Local only if the owner rules out sending note text to the provider; then use the incoming Mac Studio or keep one authenticated model service on crimson.
open_questions.evidence: options.md section 4; M4 Pro cannot rerank 50 documents with a 4B model in useful time (estimate)

open_questions.question: What happens to ClamAV?
open_questions.recommendation: Drop the resident scanner for this single-owner deployment (257 file keeps in 84 days, all from the owner's own disk, none since 2026-09-10). If scanning is required, run clamd as the one container beside Logto, accepting 1 GiB.
open_questions.evidence: not on conda-forge; 1.04 GiB resident; 257 file keeps in 84 days

open_questions.question: Drop the Grafana/Tempo/Loki/VictoriaMetrics/Alloy stack?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes. Logs and usage go to files and the lake; operator_snapshot and the console cover health. It frees 1.83 GiB and 2 GB of disk. Keep VictoriaMetrics and Grafana only if the owner wants the dashboard (about 1 GiB).
open_questions.evidence: state.md section 5; Loki's volume holds 50 kB

open_questions.question: How does Logto run on the center?
open_questions.recommendation: Pinned container first (Docker Desktop, 0.33 GiB plus the VM), with a spike package to try native Node 26 later; do not move to Logto Cloud (the issuer URL would change and every agent would have to sign in again).
open_questions.evidence: Logto has no conda-forge build; the issuer and its database must move unchanged

open_questions.question: Timing: when may the old stack be touched (L0) and when may data move (L2)?
open_questions.recommendation: L0 (recreate the stack and deploy the L0 build) can run before 2026-10-30 if the owner wants better retrieval now; L0.5 (hosted embeddings, GPU 0 idle) follows U16's go and needs the center staged; L2 not before 2026-11-17 and only after the center's PostgreSQL has soaked 7 days as control and catalog authority. If the owner wants GPU 0 earlier, run U16's golden gate on a scratch database restored from a dump on crimson (vendor extensions present there) instead of on the center.
open_questions.evidence: SERVE.md says phase 0 may precede the deadlines; the owner's 2026-10-09 note asks for no migration before 2026-11-16; five containers cannot restart cleanly until L0

open_questions.question: Wired Ethernet for the center before the move?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes; it is the owner's action (en0 exists, unused). The Wi-Fi hop to the router showed 74 ms spikes and 10.7 ms mean on 2026-10-10, and 50 to 80 percent loss on 2026-10-06; the whole memory service would depend on it.

open_questions.question: Cloudflare: a new tunnel for the center with a hostname route flip, or a second connector on the existing tunnel?
open_questions.recommendation: A new tunnel and a flip of the four hostnames (aizk, auth, admin, console). The existing tunnel's ingress names container hostnames that exist only on crimson, so a second connector would route half the traffic to nothing; the flip is atomic and its rollback is the same action.
open_questions.evidence: cloudflared runs with a remotely managed token; Caddy and Logto are reached by container name

open_questions.question: One DuckLake for evidence and AIZK history, or a second lake?
open_questions.recommendation: One lake, new table names (memory_usage, memory_events). The owner asked for 'the same ducklake'; the volumes are tiny (5,572 usage rows) and the settler already ingests files.
open_questions.evidence: design v3 allows several lakes through control.lakes, but nothing here needs a second

open_questions.question: Does the usage ledger move into DuckLake (SERVE phase 2)?
open_questions.recommendation: No: serve it from PostgreSQL (RLS, transactional enqueue, quotas) and mirror it append-only into DuckLake. It is 2.5 MB; moving it would lose row-level security for no gain.

open_questions.question: Command names: `mb serve` or `mb memory`?
open_questions.recommendation: `mb memory` for both the client verbs and service control (up, down, status, logs, doctor, migrate). `mb serve` collides with `mainboard host serve` (node-side job claimer) and the lake's serve verb.

open_questions.question: Where do offsite backups go?
open_questions.recommendation: Crimson's empty 1.8 TB SSD (/mnt/ssd2) plus /Volumes/PORTABLE. Nothing else is needed; the path carries 10.8 to 14 MB/s.
open_questions.evidence: df on crimson: /mnt/ssd1 and /mnt/ssd2 nearly empty; AIZK's current backups sit on the database's own disk and are unreadable to the crimson login

open_questions.question: Accept the written outage budgets: write freeze at most 25 minutes (15 expected), read outage at most 2 minutes, L0 at most 5 minutes, rollback freeze at most 10 minutes?
open_questions.recommendation: Accept. Expected acknowledged keeps affected: at most one, which receives a retryable error and is retried by the agent.
open_questions.evidence: usage ledger: about 1 keep an hour; restore measured at 117.7 s for 100k vectors tuned, extrapolated 6 to 8 minutes for 252k

open_questions.question: Should the extraction gate (GLiNER) be dropped entirely?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes: default off, no service. The mention detector for the web-egress sanitizer loads lazily on CPU only if web search is enabled; the ledger shows no web operation ever.
open_questions.evidence: usage_event operations; extraction costs under $3 in total
